The correct answer is neither of the listed options: the Open Door Notes were U.S. diplomatic messages (1899–1900) from Secretary of State John Hay urging powers with interests in China to keep trade access open and respect Chinese territorial and administrative integrity, opposing exclusive spheres of influence. They were not a proclamation to divide China among the US, Japan, and European empires, nor a declaration on Chinese immigration.
CONFIDENCE: 95
